devices.name: Hub Pro
notes: HouseLinc names it Central Controller.
Sold as a HomeKit bridge, which current versions of HomeKit no longer support.
Its hub interface on port 25105 is expected to match the other Hubs' but hasn't been verified.

devices.description: The central controller for an Insteon system. It drives its built-in modem over the local network, and runs scenes, schedules and alerts.
devices.name: Hub
I/O Module
notes: Has one relay, with normally open, normally closed and common contacts, and two sense inputs.
The relay's momentary mode can be set from 1 second to 30 minutes.
An I/O Module Expander, which has no Insteon radio of its own, adds four more zones.

devices.description: A wall keypad that dims and switches its connected light fixture and adds extra buttons for controlling other Insteon devices or scenes. Insteon sells it in 6-button and 8-button versions.
devices.name: Dimmer Keypad

devices.description: A small rechargeable, battery-powered wireless remote that controls Insteon devices or groups of devices. Insteon sells it in 4-scene, 8-scene, and 1-scene switch versions, and it can be wall-mounted without wiring.
devices.name: Mini Remote Control
notes: Comes as a 4-scene remote, an 8-scene remote, and a single on/off switch.
Runs on a rechargeable battery and doesn't repeat messages.

devices.description: A USB powerline modem that connects a computer to an Insteon network, so home automation software can send and receive Insteon messages.
devices.name: USB Modem
Thermostat
notes: Subcategory 0x16 is the Thermostat 2.0 firmware, given its own subcategory so software can tell its features apart; HouseLinc lists it as a heat pump thermostat.
sources: TempLinc specification rev 020 and product requirements v025

devices.name: Wireless Zone Thermostat
sources: TempLinc specification rev 020 and product requirements v025

devices.description: A small dimmer module that installs at a light fixture or behind an existing wall switch. It adds Insteon remote dimming control without replacing the original switch.
devices.name: Micro Dimmer Switch Module
notes: HouseLinc lists the regional versions as the 2442-222, 2442-422 and 2442-522.

devices.description: A small on/off relay module that installs in a fixture box or behind an existing wall switch. It adds Insteon remote control to a light while keeping the original switch.
devices.name: Micro On/Off Switch Module
notes: HouseLinc lists the regional versions as the 2443-222, 2443-422 and 2443-522.

devices.description: A small in-box module that controls 110 V motorized devices such as projection screens, shutters, and curtains. It supports several switch types and has adjustable open and close travel times.
devices.name: Micro Open/Close Module

devices.description: A plug-in module with a low-voltage sensor input and a relay output. It connects alarm sensors, door strikes, garage door openers, and other contact-closure devices to an Insteon network.
devices.name: I/O Module

devices.description: A dimmer module that mounts on a DIN rail in an electrical panel to dim and switch lighting circuits remotely. It supports adjustable brightness levels and ramp rates.
devices.name: Dimmer DIN Rail Module
notes: HouseLinc also lists its identity under 2252-222.

devices.description: A relay module that mounts on a DIN rail in an electrical panel to switch lighting circuits on and off remotely over Insteon.
devices.name: On/Off DIN Rail Module

devices.description: A plug-in module that lets a dimmable lamp be turned on and off and dimmed remotely. The lamp plugs into the module, which plugs into a wall outlet.
devices.name: Dimmer Plug
notes: Linking and unlinking modes time out after 4 minutes.
Setting the on-level to 0 turns on resume dim.

devices.name: Toggle Dimmer Switch
notes: HouseLinc lists subcategory 0x1F for firmware 0x3A and later.

devices.name: Toggle On/Off Switch
notes: HouseLinc lists subcategory 0x1A for firmware 0x3A and later.

devices.description: An in-wall duplex outlet whose top receptacle can be dimmed and switched remotely over Insteon while the bottom receptacle stays always on. It controls plug-in lamps from Insteon keypads, remotes, or the Hub.
devices.name: Dimmer Outlet
2-Wire Dimmer Switch
notes: Needs no neutral wire.
Repeats RF but not powerline.

devices.name: In-Line Dimmer Module
notes: Linked by holding SET for 10 seconds.

devices.name: In-Line Dimmer Module (Dual-Band)
notes: Returns its load and LEDs to their states before a power outage.

devices.description: A controller for dimmable lighting ballasts that use a 0-10 VDC control input. It also has two relay outputs that can switch non-dimmable ballasts of up to 5 amps each.
devices.name: 0-10V Ballast Dimmer
notes: HouseLinc names it Insteon Ballast Dimmer.
Drives a 0-10 V output and two relayed loads; on cmd1 0x11 or 0x13, cmd2 0x01 selects load 1, 0x02 load 2 and 0x03 both.
Turns on at 100% at power-up.

devices.description: A module installed inside a ceiling fan's canopy that controls the fan speed (low, medium, high) and the fan's light kit. It can be controlled by other Insteon devices or the Hub.
devices.name: Ceiling Fan and Light Control Module
In-Line On/Off Module
notes: Linked by holding SET for 10 seconds.

devices.name: On/Off Switch with Countdown Timer
notes: When its timer runs out it sends off to its group's members, unless its group control option is turned off.

devices.description: An in-wall dimmer switch that controls its light locally and can be controlled remotely by Insteon keypads, remotes, sensors, or the Hub. It is rated for up to 150 W of LED or 600 W of incandescent lighting.
devices.name: Dimmer Switch

devices.description: A higher-capacity version of the Insteon wall dimmer switch, rated for up to 250 W of dimmable LED or 1,000 W of incandescent or halogen lighting. It can be controlled locally or remotely over Insteon.
devices.name: Dimmer Switch (High Wattage)

devices.description: An in-wall on/off switch for non-dimmable loads such as fluorescent lights, ceiling fans, and exhaust fans, rated up to 17 amps. It can be controlled locally or remotely over Insteon.
devices.name: On/Off Switch
Dimmer Switch 240V
notes: Returns its load and LEDs to their states before a power outage.

devices.name: Countdown Timer Dimmer Keypad, 8 Buttons
notes: Buttons A to H start 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minute and 1 and 2 hour timers, and turn the load off.
Turns its load off for a second a minute before a timer ends, unless that's turned off.
Has one ALL-Link group.

devices.name: Dimmer Keypad, 6 Buttons
notes: Each button other than the load's can be set to toggle, send only off, or send only on.

devices.name: Dimmer Keypad, 8 Buttons
notes: Each button other than the load's can be set to toggle, send only off, or send only on.

devices.description: A wall keypad that switches its connected light fixture on and off and adds extra buttons for controlling other Insteon devices or scenes. It replaces a standard wall switch. Insteon sells it in a 6-button version.
devices.name: On/Off Keypad
notes: HouseLinc also lists its identity under 2487S-50.

devices.description: A weather-resistant plug-in relay module for switching outdoor lights and appliances on and off remotely. It is rated NEMA 3R and works from -4 to 122 degrees Fahrenheit.
devices.name: Outdoor On/Off Plug
notes: Has no X10.

devices.description: A plug-in relay module that switches lamps, fans, space heaters, and other small appliances on and off remotely. It handles loads of up to 15 amps or 1,800 W.
devices.name: On/Off Plug

devices.description: An in-wall duplex outlet with two receptacles that can each be switched on and off independently over Insteon. It is used to control plug-in lamps, fans, and small appliances.
devices.name: Dual On/Off Outlet
notes: Both outlets are switched, each by its own group.

devices.name: LED Bulb A19
notes: Has no buttons or LED.
Can be set to turn on when power returns; that's off by default.

devices.name: LED Bulb PAR38
notes: Has no buttons or LED.

devices.name: Thermostat for Heat Pump
notes: The 2441TH's hardware with heat pump firmware.
HouseLinc labels subcategories 0x13 to 0x15 as 2732-232, 2732-432 and 2732-532.
Subcategories 0x17 and 0x18 are the Thermostat 2.0 firmware, the regional versions of the 2441TH's 0x16.
HouseLinc also lists subcategories 0x0F and 0x11 for the 2732-422 and 2732-432, and 0x10 and 0x12 for the 2732-522 and 2732-532.

devices.name: Motorized Shades
notes: On opens and off closes; fast on and fast off open and close fully; brighten and dim start opening and closing, and stopping ends the movement.
Doesn't repeat Insteon messages.

devices.name: I/O Module
notes: Each relay's momentary time can be set from 0.2 seconds to 100 minutes.

devices.name: Motion Sensor
notes: HouseLinc also lists its US identity under the 2420M.

devices.description: A wireless, battery-powered sensor that mounts on a door or window and reports when it opens or closes. It can switch Insteon lights or, with the Hub, send phone alerts.
devices.name: Open/Close Sensor
notes: HouseLinc lists subcategory 0x09 as the Door Sensor 2843-232.
sources: Insteon command workbook, HeartBeat Status sheet

devices.description: A wireless, battery-powered motion sensor that can turn Insteon-controlled lights on when someone enters a room and off after they leave.
devices.name: Motion Sensor II
notes: Groups other than 1 are off by default.
Its heartbeat's cmd1, 0x11 to 0x14, gives the battery level from fully charged to almost empty.
Optional groups report temperature and light levels.
sources: 2844-x22 Motion Sensor II and III PRDs

devices.description: A wireless, battery-powered sensor recessed into a door frame that reports when the door opens or closes. It can trigger lights and other Insteon devices.
devices.name: Hidden Door Sensor
notes: Sends closed to group 2 only when set to.
Sends a heartbeat at most every 24 hours; its PRD leaves the group undecided.

devices.description: A battery-powered sensor placed on the floor near sinks, toilets, washing machines, or water heaters that signals when it detects water. With an Insteon Hub or siren it can send alerts.
devices.name: Leak Sensor
notes: Its heartbeat sends on when dry and off when wet.
Once wet, it ignores further changes until its SET button is pressed.
sources: Insteon command workbook, HeartBeat Status sheet

devices.name: ICON Dimmer Module
notes: HouseLinc also lists its identity under 2856D2B.

devices.name: Deadbolt
notes: It's asleep most of the time, so it may take a few seconds to answer a command.

devices.name: Smoke Bridge
notes: HouseLinc names it Smoke Detector.
It sends Insteon messages over powerline only; its radio only listens for the smoke alarms it's paired with.
Tapping its SET button sends each group's command as a test, ending with the all-clear.
It sends a heartbeat to group 0x0A, which software can turn off; its interval isn't documented.

devices.name: Range Extender
notes: Repeats Insteon messages between powerline and RF, and bridges the two powerline phases.
Answers status requests and beeps; it has no load to control.
